product.title: From a request
product.intro: PraxisForge brings evidence, specialist agents and human review into one place. Follow the work from its first brief to an inspectable outcome.

sections.title: One continuous thread.

items.title: Give the work a clear brief
items.body: Describe the client, the deliverable and the evidence the team may use. A request begins as a durable task, with its own history and an explicit outcome.

items.title: Bring the right context
items.body: Versioned text sources give the specialists something concrete to work from. Source references travel with the proposed draft so the reviewer can inspect its basis.

items.title: Review the exact proposal
items.body: Read the message, intended recipient, account and commitments together. Approval belongs to that specific action and its evidence; a changed proposal needs a new decision.

items.title: Keep an inspectable result
items.body: The bounded core records an approved draft and internal commitments together, then produces a receipt. Download the resulting JSON artifact for your own review or handoff.

sections.intro: A useful outcome needs more than a fluent answer. It needs context, a deliberate decision and a record of what actually happened.

items.title: The Orchestrator
items.body: Turns the request into a bounded plan. It identifies the deliverable, the missing information and the work each specialist needs to do.

items.title: The Researcher
items.body: Checks the selected evidence for supported commitments and unresolved details. It brings source references into the handoff instead of treating confidence as evidence.

items.title: The Operator
items.body: Prepares the proposed draft and commitments for review. In this bounded core, it has no tools for sending email, browsing accounts or administering systems.

items.title: A public design preview
items.body: The interactive workspace uses synthetic client records. Filters, task details and approval interactions demonstrate the experience; its actions are simulated.

items.title: An authenticated operations core
items.body: The owner-operated core implements text knowledge, durable tasks, exact approvals and internal receipts. It is a bounded implementation under verification, with no public registration.

items.title: External tools, deliberately later
items.body: Email delivery, connected drives, messaging and third-party CRM writes are planned connector work. Familiar tool names describe the direction, not an active account connection.

sections.title: Built for work you can inspect.
paragraphs: PraxisForge starts with one concrete agency workflow: turn meeting and procedure evidence into a thoughtful follow-up draft and a clear set of commitments. That focus makes it possible to test the handoffs, review the proposed changes and distinguish a completed internal action from a failed or blocked attempt.

The larger platform direction includes more connectors, richer retrieval and measured improvements to specialist behavior. Those capabilities belong on the roadmap until their permissions, failure handling and verification are implemented.

sections.title: The foundations of considered operations.

items.title: A calm operational workspace
items.body: Inspect tasks, sources, agents and approval states through a focused interface. The public workspace makes the workflow explorable with synthetic records.

items.title: Versioned text knowledge
items.body: The bounded core stores source text with versions and content hashes. Drafts reference the selected evidence so a reviewer can check what informed them.

items.title: Durable task history
items.body: Requests, attempts, stages and outcomes are recorded in the core. Failure and cancellation remain visible instead of disappearing behind an optimistic success message.

items.title: Exact approval envelopes
items.body: Approval binds the task, actor, workspace, account, recipient, draft, commitments, source hashes and expiry. The core rejects changes that no longer match the reviewed proposal.

items.title: Internal commitments and receipts
items.body: Approved internal work records its draft and commitments with a receipt. A downloaded JSON artifact retains the approved action and evidence references.

items.title: Three specialist roles
items.body: Coordinator, researcher and operator responsibilities run through a bounded Hermes integration. Inference uses a configured local model, with external tools disabled in this implementation.

sections.intro: Available means you can explore it in the public preview. Limited means it exists in the owner-operated core and is not an unrestricted public service.

items.title: Email delivery
items.body: Sending from a real mailbox will need scoped authorization, account selection, exact-message approval and a verifiable provider outcome. No external email is sent by the current core.

items.title: Connected document libraries
items.body: Account-authorized file discovery and ingestion are future work. Current knowledge input is bounded text; a connected-drive logo is not evidence that files are being synchronized.

items.title: Messaging and CRM platforms
items.body: Third-party channels and CRM writes remain separate integration milestones. Current commitments are internal platform records, not synchronized records in an external CRM.

items.title: Richer knowledge retrieval
items.body: Document formats, semantic retrieval and knowledge graphs need evaluation before they can extend the evidence boundary. Current source selection should remain understandable.

items.title: Measured improvement
items.body: Prompt, skill and model changes should beat a measured baseline before promotion. An isolated research environment is part of the direction, not a capability claimed by this preview.

items.title: Stronger customer isolation
items.body: Independent customer admission requires further identity, execution, credential and recovery controls. Workspace scoping in the bounded core does not establish hostile-tenant isolation.

items.title: Can an agent send a message on its own?
items.body: No external delivery connector is configured in the bounded core. It can prepare a draft for review and record an approved internal action; a receipt does not claim that an email was delivered.

items.title: Is the public workspace connected to real customer data?
items.body: The public design preview contains synthetic records and simulated actions. Authenticated operations is a separate interface with its own access boundary.

items.title: Does local inference make every answer correct?
items.body: No. Model output still needs validation and human judgment. Inspect sources, missing details and the exact proposal before approving work.

sections.title: A brief worth giving the team.

items.title: The request
items.body: Review these discovery notes and the client follow-up procedure. Prepare a concise next-step draft and list only the commitments the evidence supports.

items.title: The evidence
items.body: Select the meeting notes and the relevant procedure as text sources. Give each source a meaningful title, check its current version and leave unrelated client context out of the request.

items.title: The review
items.body: Read the proposed message beside its sources. Confirm the account, recipient and commitments. If a date or owner is uncertain, resolve it before approving rather than asking the system to guess.

items.title: The result
items.body: An approved internal draft, recorded commitments and an inspectable receipt. External delivery remains a separate human or future connector action.

items.title: A path to broader workflows

about.title: More intention
about.intro: PraxisForge is an independently built exploration of a practical question: what makes an AI-assisted business outcome understandable enough to trust?

sections.title: The gap between an answer and an outcome.
paragraphs: A fluent response can make work feel complete before anything has been verified. A useful operational system needs a more concrete trail: the request, the evidence it was allowed to use, the person who approved the proposed action and a record of the result.

PraxisForge begins there. It brings specialist roles into a workspace designed around deliberate handoffs, visible boundaries and human judgment. The first bounded workflow focuses on agency follow-up drafts and internal commitments, where both the context and the decision can be inspected.

items.title: Context before confidence
items.body: A recommendation should point back to its permitted sources. Missing evidence deserves a clear blocked outcome, not a more persuasive sentence.

items.title: Judgment before execution
items.body: The reviewer should see the actual proposal. Approval should mean a specific decision about a specific action, with a defined account, recipient and evidence boundary.

items.title: Evidence after action
items.body: An outcome needs a record. Internal changes and external provider acceptance are different claims; the product should make that distinction legible.

items.title: Calm throughout
items.body: Clear typography, considered pacing and restrained motion help people inspect work. The interface should give attention back to the decision that matters.

security.title: Control belongs
security.intro: Clear permission boundaries, exact approvals and inspectable outcomes guide the bounded core. This page describes implementation choices and limits, not a certification.

sections.title: A deliberate boundary around each decision.

items.title: Authenticated operations
items.body: The core requires owner sign-in and applies workspace membership checks to its resources. The public synthetic workspace is a separate demonstration and does not grant access to core records.

items.title: Approval for the exact action
items.body: Task, actor, workspace, account, recipient, content, commitments, sources and expiry are part of the approval boundary. A changed or stale proposal must not reuse an earlier approval.

items.title: Evidence treated as data
items.body: Source text is untrusted context. It cannot grant an agent new permissions or authorize external actions. Structured model outputs are validated before business state changes.

items.title: Restricted specialist execution
items.body: The bounded integration uses a configured local model with agent tools disabled. The specialist roles have no supported path for sending email, browsing accounts or administering the host.

sections.title: Know what happened. Know the remaining work.

items.title: Internal changes with a receipt
items.body: Approved drafts and commitments are recorded together with their internal receipt. The record describes that internal action; it is not a provider delivery confirmation.

items.title: Visible unsuccessful outcomes
items.body: Tasks can fail, block, cancel or require a new decision. The interface should show those outcomes without quietly relabeling them as completion.

items.title: Recovery is an evidence gate
items.body: An encrypted off-host production backup restored successfully into a fresh isolated database, with matching schema and business records. This is a logical database restore test; full host recovery, scheduled backups and recovery-time or recovery-point guarantees remain outside this release.

items.title: Independent customer isolation
items.body: Workspace authorization is part of the core. Admission of unrelated customers still needs further isolation, identity, credential and operating review.

items.title: External connector permissions
items.body: Mailbox, drive, messaging and third-party CRM access are not configured capabilities. Each future connector needs its own scope, authorization, failure handling and verification.

items.title: Formal assurance
items.body: No SOC 2, ISO certification, penetration-test attestation or regulatory-compliance claim is made here. The presence of technical controls is not a substitute for independent assurance.

sections.title: Evaluate with care.
paragraphs: Use synthetic or non-sensitive material while evaluating the product. Read the exact proposal and its sources before making a decision. Do not assume a model’s answer is correct because it is detailed or confident.

Do not place passwords, access tokens or unrelated personal information into source text. Product browsing does not create a confidentiality, support or managed-service agreement. Review the privacy and terms notices for the current public experience.

items.title: Does local inference mean no data is processed?
items.body: No. The authenticated core processes the request and selected evidence in its configured environment. Public hosting and edge services also handle web requests; the privacy notice explains the public experience.

items.title: Can I use this for regulated or critical decisions?
items.body: The preview is not offered as a validated regulated decision system. A deployment would need a specific risk assessment, operating controls and applicable professional or legal review.

items.title: How should I raise a concern?
items.body: The contact page describes the current communication route. Share a concise description without including passwords, private keys or other people’s sensitive information.

sections.title: A five-minute tour of the preview.

items.title: Find a task
items.body: Browse the task list, use the search field and narrow the view by status. The records are illustrative examples of agency work.

items.title: Inspect the detail
items.body: Open a task to see its proposed action and activity. Switch to Evidence to inspect the supporting source preview where one is available.

items.title: Review the proposal
items.body: Check the account, recipient, subject and message together. Approve or reject in the demo to see how the decision changes the simulated state.

items.title: Reset and compare
items.body: Reset the demo to return to its initial sample state. Try another request or explore the agent, knowledge and connector views; connector descriptions remain a design preview.

sections.title: The bounded core workflow.

items.title: Sign in to operations
items.body: Use only the configured operator account. After sign-in, confirm the workspace before adding evidence or submitting work.

items.title: Add selected text evidence
items.body: Give each source a meaningful title and provide the relevant bounded text. Keep credentials and unrelated sensitive data out of the content. Check the source you intend to use before creating a request.

items.title: Submit a specific request
items.body: Describe the client and desired draft, select the supporting documents and check the intended recipient/account. The request becomes a durable task.

items.title: Watch the actual outcome
items.body: Stages and history show the work as it proceeds. A local model can take time. A blocked or failed task is an outcome to inspect, not an instruction to assume success or repeatedly submit the same work.

items.title: Review the exact action
items.body: Read the draft, commitments and evidence together. Approve only a supported, current proposal. Reject or cancel when the proposed action should not proceed.

items.title: Inspect and download the receipt
items.body: After a completed internal action, inspect its receipt and download the JSON artifact. It retains the approved action and source hashes. It does not confirm external email delivery.

sections.intro: These steps describe the implemented owner-operated core. Public availability and production verification are tracked separately on the status page.

sections.title: A status is part of the record.

items.title: Queued or running
items.body: The task is waiting or being processed. Stage, attempt and history provide context; the request is not yet a completed result.

items.title: Awaiting approval
items.body: A proposal is ready for a person to inspect. No approved internal action has been committed yet.

items.title: Completed
items.body: The approved internal draft and commitments have been recorded with a receipt. Read its verification text for the exact outcome.

items.title: Blocked, failed or cancelled
items.body: The work could not proceed, encountered an error or was stopped. Inspect the reason and history before deciding whether to provide better evidence or create a new request.

items.title: Check the identity
items.body: Confirm the client, account and intended recipient. An otherwise useful draft can still be wrong for the person or context it names.

items.title: Check the support
items.body: Read the cited sources and check names, dates, owners and commitments. Do not fill an evidence gap with an assumption.

items.title: Check the scope
items.body: Understand that the current core records an internal draft and commitments. Sending or synchronizing externally requires a separately supported connector.

items.title: Check the result
items.body: Keep the receipt and approved artifact if you need to review or hand off the work. Treat a download as a record, not a claim that every later action has happened.

items.title: Restricted operations
items.body: Authorized access uses account identifiers, a password hash, and server-side session records. Tasks, supplied knowledge, execution events, approvals, results, and evidence can be stored as durable business records. This area is reserved for controlled testing; it is not open customer registration.

sections.title: Why information is used.
paragraphs: The preview uses information to deliver pages, authenticate authorized access, protect the service, investigate failures, maintain test records, and respond to requests. The current operations configuration runs model inference on the self-hosted environment; it has no configured fallback to an external model API. That does not mean the public website is disconnected from hosting, edge, or email providers.

Where a law requires a lawful basis, that basis depends on the purpose: service or pre-contract requests, legitimate operational and security interests subject to the required balancing, legal obligations, or consent for a genuinely optional use where required. Browsing this notice is not blanket consent.

sections.title: Services and disclosures.
paragraphs: The operator and relevant infrastructure or email providers may process information needed for their role. Cloudflare handles edge delivery and security; email you send is processed by the email providers involved. Information may also be disclosed where legally required or necessary to address abuse, protect rights, or investigate a security incident.

The application has no implemented advertising network, data-broker sale, or cross-site advertising feature. No claim is made that every edge diagnostic is disabled. Optional analytics or new integrations require a review of the notice, provider arrangements, and any necessary user choices before use.

sections.title: Retention and deletion.
paragraphs: Authentication cookies expire after eight hours unless removed sooner. Other data does not have one universal automatic deletion period in this preview. Retention of correspondence, request logs, test records, and backups depends on the relevant system and operational need; a finalized customer retention schedule is not yet available.

Removing a knowledge document from retrieval clears its active content from that retrieval path. It does not automatically erase earlier task snapshots, results, audit records, or backup copies. There is no complete self-service account erasure or export workflow. Ask the operator for a review of specific information; the response will explain what can be removed, what must be retained, and any technical limits.

sections.title: Location and transfers.
paragraphs: The hosted preview, edge network, and email services may process information in more than one country. This notice does not promise EU-only or US-only residency. Before a customer deployment that requires regional restrictions or international-transfer safeguards, the actual providers, locations, contractual measures, and applicable requirements must be agreed.

sections.title: EU and EEA requests.
paragraphs: Where GDPR applies, you may have rights to access, correct, erase, restrict, object to processing, or receive portable data, depending on the processing and legal conditions. Consent can be withdrawn for future consent-based processing. You can also raise a concern with a competent data protection authority. The demonstration is not offered for decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects about people.

sections.title: US and California requests.
paragraphs: Privacy rights vary across US states and depend on whether the relevant law covers the activity. Where California law applies, rights can include knowing, deleting, correcting, and opting out of covered sale or sharing, limiting certain sensitive-information uses, and receiving non-discriminatory treatment for exercising rights. Applicable opt-out signals, including Global Privacy Control, must be respected where legally required. The current application does not implement advertising sale or sharing.
The application does not alter its behavior in response to the browser’s legacy Do Not Track header. That disclosure does not limit any obligation to honor a legally recognized privacy signal.

sections.title: Make a request.
paragraphs: Email muhammadzahidulislam2222@gmail.com with the nature of your request and enough context to locate the relevant information. Avoid sending identity documents unless a proportionate verification method is agreed. The operator may need to confirm your identity or authority without revealing another person’s data. Requests will be handled within the deadlines applicable to the circumstances; reasons and available options will be explained if a request cannot be fulfilled.

sections.title: Children and sensitive information.
paragraphs: This is a business-operations demonstration, not a service directed to children. Do not submit children’s information, health records, payment credentials, identity documents, or other regulated or highly sensitive data. Contact the operator if such information may have been submitted. Security controls reduce risk; they do not eliminate it.

cta.title: A privacy question is welcome.
cta.text: Describe the data or interaction you are concerned about. You do not need an account to contact the operator.

terms.title: Explore responsibly.
terms.intro: The practical terms for browsing and testing the PraxisForge AI preview.

notice.label: Updated 15 October 2026 · Public demonstration
notice.text: This preview has no paid checkout, customer service-level agreement, or general production-use offer. Any future paid engagement requires a separate written agreement.

sections.title: What you may explore.
paragraphs: You may browse the public pages and interact with the illustrative workspace for evaluation. Access to the restricted operations area requires the operator’s permission and valid credentials. Do not attempt to enter another workspace, discover credentials, bypass controls, or access information you are not authorized to see.

sections.title: Responsible use.
paragraphs: Do not disrupt the service, send malicious content, impersonate others, infringe rights, or use the preview for unlawful activity. Test only data and systems you are authorized to use. Responsible security reports are welcome through the contact page; do not expose other people’s data or continue testing after identifying a vulnerability that could harm the service.

sections.title: AI output needs review.
paragraphs: AI-generated plans, summaries, drafts, and recommendations can be incomplete, inaccurate, or unsuitable. Illustrative records and simulated approvals are demonstrations, not proof that an external action occurred. A real result needs appropriate evidence and verification.

Review source material, recipients, accounts, content, and permissions before approving a consequential action. The preview is not provided for medical, legal, financial, employment, credit, or other regulated decisions, and it is not professional advice.

sections.title: Your information and project materials.
paragraphs: You retain rights you already have in material you lawfully provide. Providing material authorizes only the processing reasonably necessary for the interaction you requested, subject to the privacy notice; it does not grant unrestricted rights to publish it or train a model on it. Use synthetic examples here rather than confidential information.

The project’s branding, artwork, interface, and content may be protected by intellectual-property rights. These website terms do not grant a license to redistribute the software or third-party assets. Where software or an asset is separately released under a license, that license governs it.

sections.title: Third-party technology.
paragraphs: Hermes Agent, model software, cloud platforms, and integration names remain subject to their own licenses and terms. Mentioning them does not imply that their providers endorse PraxisForge AI. A link to another service does not extend this preview’s terms to that service.

sections.title: Availability and changes.
paragraphs: The preview may be changed, paused, restricted, or withdrawn while it is developed. It has no guaranteed uptime, support response time, recovery objective, or preservation period. Keep your own copies of anything you need. Planned features and deployment options describe direction rather than a commitment to deliver on a particular date.
If access must be limited to address misuse or security risk, the operator may do so. Privacy requests and rights that apply by law remain available.

sections.title: Expectations and mandatory rights.
paragraphs: The demonstration is provided for evaluation in its current state. No promise is made that its outputs are error-free, suitable for a particular business purpose, or sufficient for compliance. These terms do not exclude liability or remedies that cannot lawfully be excluded, and they do not remove mandatory consumer or data-protection rights.

A future commercial agreement must identify the parties, scope, fees, operating responsibilities, governing law, and dispute arrangements. No exclusive court, arbitration requirement, or governing jurisdiction is imposed through this preview notice.

sections.title: Questions and revisions.
paragraphs: Questions about permitted use can be sent to muhammadzahidulislam2222@gmail.com. Revisions will be dated on this page. A materially different service, data use, or commercial arrangement needs clear notice and, where required, a separate agreement or choice.

cta.title: Discuss the use case first.
cta.text: If you want to evaluate this for a real team, start with scope, data boundaries, and what success would mean.

cookies.title: Small files.
cookies.intro: How the preview uses browser storage and how to control it.

notice.label: Updated 15 October 2026
notice.text: This notice explains current behavior. It is not a request for consent to optional tracking, and continuing to browse is not treated as that consent.

items.title: __Host-praxis-session
items.body: Created after a successful authorized login. Links the browser to a server-side authenticated session. Maximum age: eight hours. Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, with the root path.

items.title: __Host-praxis-csrf
items.body: Created with authorized login to support request-integrity checks for state-changing operations. Maximum age: eight hours. Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, with the root path.

sections.title: Authentication and security.
paragraphs: These application cookies support the restricted operations area. They are not advertising identifiers. Secure limits transmission to HTTPS; HttpOnly prevents access through ordinary page JavaScript; SameSite=Strict restricts cross-site delivery. Logging out removes the application cookies and invalidates the server-side session.

sections.title: Cloudflare and the website edge.
paragraphs: Cloudflare sits between the browser and the host for delivery and security. Depending on the security features and challenges encountered, it may set its own cookies, such as a challenge-clearance cookie. Those cookies and their lifetimes are controlled by the enabled provider features rather than the application login settings. Cloudflare also receives request and connection metadata.

The application code does not implement advertising cookies or an optional analytics library. Edge-managed measurement is a separate configuration concern. Nonessential tracking must not be treated as necessary simply because it is supplied by an infrastructure provider; any future optional tracking needs appropriate information and consent where required.

sections.title: Public demo and local storage.
paragraphs: The public workspace uses illustrative records in page memory. The application does not persist those demo edits in localStorage or sessionStorage. The current view may be reflected in the URL. Browser caches and ordinary network requests still exist; an in-memory demo does not mean the browser or infrastructure handles no information.

sections.title: Your choices.
paragraphs: You can inspect, remove, or block cookies through your browser settings. Blocking authentication cookies prevents the restricted operations login from working. Blocking security cookies can trigger repeated challenges or prevent access. Removing a browser cookie does not erase server-side records.

There is no optional-cookie preference panel in this preview. Do not interpret that as consent to advertising or analytics. Contact the operator if you see an unexpected cookie or want a current explanation of the website’s storage behavior.

cta.title: Found something unexpected?
cta.text: Send the cookie name and page where it appeared. Do not include the cookie value.

accessibility.title: Built to be explored.
accessibility.intro: Our approach to access, motion, keyboard interaction, and continued evaluation.

notice.label: Updated 15 October 2026 · Work in progress
notice.text: WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the design target. This is not a declaration of full conformance or a certification under US or EU accessibility law.

items.title: Keyboard access
items.body: Navigation and controls use semantic elements, visible focus states, and a skip link to the main content. Interactive dialogs are designed to be usable without a pointer.

items.title: Motion preferences
items.body: The interface responds to the operating system’s reduced-motion preference. Smooth scrolling and animation are enhancements; essential information should remain available without them.

items.title: Readable structure
items.body: Pages use meaningful headings, explicit control names, responsive layouts, and text alternatives where appropriate. Visual presentation should support the content rather than replace it.

sections.title: How access is evaluated.
paragraphs: Development checks include automated accessibility scans, keyboard interaction, responsive viewport inspection, and reduced-motion behavior. Automated checks find only some barriers. They do not establish that every page, assistive technology, zoom level, or interaction is accessible.

The current multi-page expansion requires its own checks. No independent accessibility certification or complete assistive-technology audit has been completed. Evaluation results must be tied to the version and screens actually tested.

sections.title: Known limits.
paragraphs: Complex task dialogs, dense operational information, animated visual effects, and third-party security challenges need continued manual assessment. A blocked security challenge or an inaccessible provider interface can prevent access even when the application page is usable. Please report the exact step where access becomes difficult.

sections.title: Report an access barrier.
paragraphs: Email muhammadzahidulislam2222@gmail.com with the page, action you were trying to complete, and a description of the barrier. If useful, include your browser and assistive technology; do not send sensitive records or credentials. You may ask for the information in a simpler text format.
The operator will review the report and discuss a practical alternative where possible. There is no published response-time guarantee, but accessibility feedback is used to prioritize corrections.

sections.title: Standards and applicable requirements.
paragraphs: WCAG is a technical reference for improving accessibility. Legal duties depend on the service, operator, jurisdiction, and circumstances. This statement does not claim blanket ADA or European Accessibility Act compliance, and it does not limit any rights you have under applicable law.

cta.title: Help make the next version better.
cta.text: A precise description of the barrier is more useful than a score. Tell us where the experience stopped working for you.

common.contactText: For product questions or a scoped deployment discussion, email a short description of the workflow. Keep passwords, private client records and sensitive attachments out of the first message.
